correctness.rationale: The reduction to endpoints is valid by strict convexity and full-dimensional coordinate boxes (t>0); for a chosen signed edge orientation, maximizing independent box signs yields sum_v(|outdeg-indeg|+t)^2. On a bipartite unicyclic graph exactly two all-pure source/sink orientations saturate every coordinate. On an odd cycle at least one cycle vertex is mixed; the single-vertex square loss is >=4(deg(v)+t-1), and a one-defect alternating cycle orientation with attached tree edges consistently oriented realizes equality at any minimum-degree cycle vertex. Equality forces exactly one such defect, giving four distinct contacts per defect, also when defect degree two because the zero-imbalance box sign doubles the two cycle choices. Center 0 follows from antipodal radius equality; diameter endpoints are antipodal contacts. Independently constructed signed-endpoint searches checked C3,C4,C5 and a branched triangle at positive integer t, matching radius and contact counts. The finite search does not prove all unicyclic graphs or real t.
